summary: Resolve three automated-review findings: collide-free TOML tag for the second auth env var, single required MCP credential, and an XML-correct default Accept header.
reason: The generated CLI exposes two interchangeable bearer env vars (BGG_TOKEN and its BOARDGAMEGEEK_TOKEN alias). The print derived an identical `toml:"token"` tag for both Config fields, so go-toml/v2 last-wins made BggToken unserializable and risked duplicate `token =` keys corrupting a saved config; the MCP manifest also marked both aliases required, forcing the same secret to be entered twice; and the if-empty Accept default was application/json on an XML-only API, so any direct client call (outside the promoted commands that set an application/xml headerOverride) could draw a 406.
validated_outcome: go build ./... and go vet ./... pass. config.go now tags BoardgamegeekToken as toml:"boardgamegeek_token" (distinct from BggToken's toml:"token"), so both round-trip independently and env-var bearer auth is unchanged. manifest.json marks only bgg_token required (boardgamegeek_token is an optional alias). client.go defaults Accept to application/xml for this XML-only API while binary responses still negotiate */*.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Generator-level dedupe of credential-field TOML tags when two auth env vars share a suffix (e.g. BGG_TOKEN + BOARDGAMEGEEK_TOKEN both reduce to `token` via EnvVarPlaceholder).
deferred_to_upstream.reason: credentialFields() derives each tag from the env-var suffix and does not detect collisions, so any multi-alias bearer auth prints two struct fields with the same toml tag. The fix belongs in cli-printing-press credentialFields(), not per-CLI.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Generator-level XML-aware Accept default (now landed upstream): client.go.tmpl defaults the if-empty Accept header to application/xml when the spec HasXMLResponse.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Carried as a patch here because the published print predates the cli-printing-press change; regenerating against a press that includes the XML Accept default reproduces this byte-for-byte.
